_readme: WHO HIRED YOU. You are a professional tidier; every campaign level is a job.
A client turns up at the start of one, says a line or two, and comes back at
the end to thank you. They recur: a client's stages are a story arc.
levels.json is the CONFIG (rooms, locks, tips). This file is the VOICE.
A stage can never change how a level plays — it only claims one by id.
RULES (checked at boot — a violation shows an error screen, not a silent bug):
1. Every level in levels.json is claimed by exactly ONE stage. Two claims
would put the level on the board twice and give the note two voices;
no claim would open a job with nobody there and hide it from the board.
2. A stage must name a level that exists, and a client's stages must run
FORWARD through levels.json — they are listed in play order, and out of
order the pips fill in backwards.
3. Every client needs an emoji; every stage needs intro and outro lines.
4. A client with no stages is only legal with "soon": true — that is how a
future client appears on the board as a silhouette.
ARCS INTERLEAVE. Another client can be hired between two of yours; that is
what makes them feel like people with their own lives. Marguerite pauses
while the frat house happens, then comes back at the very end.
THE NEXT-JOB CARD carries two of these, and they are not interchangeable:
hook   — THE CLIENT TALKING TO YOU. First person, direct address, in their
own voice, about the RELATIONSHIP: how they got hold of you, or
what having worked for you once has changed. Not the narrator.
A draft of these was third person and it was accurate and inert:
the referral is the funniest thing most of these people have to
offer, and reported rather than told it stops being a joke. An
alien watched you through a window for a month; a parrot got your
number out of a bin; a gorilla lifted it off the parrot's desk; a
robot was handed your details by a frat boy and cannot parse the
compliment. Say it in their mouth.
A FIRST stage is a referral, and the referrals CHAIN across the
whole cast on purpose — Mom to Marguerite to Sam; a pizza box to the
frat to Unit 7 to Dr. Ashworth; Zorb to Nettle; Captain to Boris.
That chain is the only thing making eleven clients feel like one
world rather than eleven jobs.
DO NOT write the job into it. A draft did, and because the teaser
below already says what they want, the card printed the same
sentence twice on thirteen levels. Two lines on a phone, maximum.
teaser — THEIR OWN WORDS, quoted. These existed on every stage from the
start and NOTHING RENDERED THEM until the card did: the only reader
asked for a client-level teaser field that no client has.
Thirty-four authored lines, boot-validated for tokens the whole
time, and invisible. Add a field here, render it in the same change.
A stage with no hook falls back to the level blurb, and boot warns about it.
TOKENS. intro/outro/teaser/hook: {handSlots} {rowLen} {name} {level}
note text/reply:    {container} {room} {handSlots} {rowLen} {name}
(a room and container are only known once one is finished)
NOTES are a LIST, one per room that leaves you one, in the order rooms are
finished — not room order. Keep each one room-agnostic apart from its tokens.
A level with one container (1-1) never drops a note at all; put those words
in the intro. Omit `note` and the room-authored copy in quests.json is used
instead, signed by this client either way.
VOICE. Dry, warm, short. One or two sentences. The frat types in lower case
because they are texting you; Zorb does not use contractions. Nobody in this
game shouts, except the frat, once, about the Dean.
MOM IS THE PROLOGUE and the only person here who isn't a client — the first
two levels are your own room, which is why she can teach the verbs without a
word of tutorial voice. Two stages is deliberate: she exists to hand you to
Marguerite, and validate.js allows a two-stage arc for exactly that.

clients.name: Mom
clients.waiting: She has a list. She always has a list.
clients.farewell: She still sends you photos of the garage.

stages.hook: You asked me for a summer job. I have one for you. It is upstairs and it is yours.
stages.teaser: "I'm not asking again."
intro: You want to make money this summer? Wonderful. You can start with your own room.
Three things on this floor. One place they go. I believe in you.
outro: There's a carpet under there. I always suspected.

stages.hook: I looked at it again this morning. Sweetheart. Come back up here.
stages.teaser: "A pile is not a system."
stages.replay: Again? It'll be like this by Thursday anyway.
intro: Better. Now the part where things go where they actually belong.
A pile is not a system, sweetheart.
outro: Look at that. You're genuinely good at this.
So I told my friend Marguerite about you. She's clearing out her grandmother's house and she's drowning. Expect a call.

note.text: While you're in here: anything that lives in the {container} goes back in the {container}.
note.reply: Was that so hard? Don't answer that.

clients.name: Marguerite
clients.waiting: She says she's fine. She is not fine.
clients.farewell: The house sold in a week. She kept the clock.

stages.hook: Your mom rang me about you. I am in my grandmother’s house, I have been for an hour, and I have not picked up one thing.
stages.teaser: "Your mother said you'd know what to do."
intro: Your mom said you were looking to make some money this summer.
This was my grandmother's house. I've been standing in it for an hour and I haven't picked up one thing.
outro: There's a door in there I've had shut since March.
You walked through it like it was nothing. Thank you.

note.text: If the {container} is as bad as I think it is, just do what you can.
note.reply: Better than I'd have managed. Thank you.

stages.hook: I kept your number. There are three more rooms in here and I have almost stopped apologising for them.
stages.teaser: "It's getting easier. Slightly."
intro: Three rooms this time. I've almost stopped apologising for the state of it.
Almost.
outro: The estate agent comes Tuesday. Because of you I'm going to let her in.

note.text: The {room} is where she actually lived. The {container} first, if you don't mind.
note.reply: The {container}, done. That was the one that mattered.

note.text: Whatever's left in here goes in the {container}. She was never sentimental about storage.
note.reply: Sorted. She'd have approved of the efficiency.

stages.hook: It has been months and the house has sold. I asked for you because I could not ask anybody else.
stages.teaser: "One last room. I couldn't face it alone."
intro: The house sold. Completed on Friday.
There's one room I never opened while she was alive, and I'm not opening it by myself.
outro: Photographs. Forty years of them, in date order.
Of course she had a system. Thank you for staying.

note.text: Anything that looks like it mattered — the {container}. I'll go through it at home.
note.reply: I'll go through it at home. Thank you for not making me do it here.

clients.name: Delta Tau Chi
clients.waiting: They've gone quiet. That's usually worse.
clients.farewell: They got the deposit back. All of it. They were genuinely stunned.
clients._note: Every one of these jobs is theme: frat — the first world in the game that is not the house and not a dream. It arrives at 3-1 because that is when they arrive, which is the whole design: a world should turn up because somebody hired you into it.

stages.hook: hey so somebody wrote your number on a pizza box and honestly thank god. six of us. one deposit.
stages.teaser: "this was like this when we moved in"
intro: hey so. this was like this when we moved in.
the last guys were animals. we would never live like this.
outro: yeah that's so much better. we're gonna keep it like this.

note.text: if you find the keys to the {container} let us know, we've been guessing for a week
note.reply: you got it open. nobody has seen inside that thing since september

stages.hook: you’re in the group chat now. under a name we are not going to tell you.
stages.teaser: "ok that was ONE party. one."
stages.replay: you again. we're not even embarrassed anymore.
intro: ok before you say anything: that was one party.
one. it is not going to happen again.
outro: you're a legend. that is not going to happen again.

note.text: whatever's in the {container} isn't ours. we're not asking. you don't have to either
note.reply: we are all agreeing that the {container} was always like that

stages.hook: we’re not even getting up to let you in anymore. door’s open. help yourself.
stages.teaser: "same as last time. you know where it goes."
intro: same as last time. you know where everything goes.
we've stopped pretending this is unusual.
outro: honestly at this point you know this house better than we do.

note.text: the {container}. don't ask. thank you
note.reply: the {container}. we owe you one.

note.text: if the {room} smells, that's a known issue
note.reply: the {room} does not smell anymore. incredible

stages.hook: sorry it’s 11pm. we need you. it is not an emergency. it is completely an emergency.
stages.teaser: "the Dean is coming FRIDAY"
intro: the Dean is coming friday. FRIDAY.
he brings a clipboard. he has used it before.
outro: he walked the whole house and said 'huh'. that's a win. that's a huge win.

note.text: the {container} is the first thing he opens. he always opens the {container}
note.reply: he opened the {container} and said nothing. perfect

stages.hook: last one man. we want the person who has seen this place at its absolute worst. that’s you. affectionately.
stages.teaser: "deposit day. it all rides on this."
intro: last one. we're moving out.
if we get the deposit back you're invited to the next one. sorry. sorry.
outro: we got all of it back. ALL of it.
the landlord asked who our cleaner was. we said you were unavailable. we're keeping you.

note.text: the {container} has to look like nobody ever touched it. good luck
note.reply: the {container} looks brand new. how

clients.name: Zorb
clients.waiting: Zorb is compiling. Zorb will return.
clients.farewell: The report was submitted. Zorb scored 4 out of 10 and considers this a triumph. He kept the horse.

stages.hook: I have watched you working through a window, three houses distant, for one of your months. I have questions. Come.
stages.teaser: "I have sealed a room. I no longer recall why."
intro: I have been assigned this dwelling for one of your years.
I have sealed a room. I no longer recall why. The keys are in here somewhere.
outro: The room is open. It contained nothing of interest. I am relieved and also disappointed.

note.text: Place the objects inside the {container}. I have observed your species doing this and I do not know why.
note.reply: The {container} is full and I feel nothing. I am told this is normal.

_note: THE FIRST LEVEL THAT IS NOT A BUILDING. Zorb's first job (4-1) is the
dwelling he was assigned, because meeting an alien in a beige house is
the joke; his second is his own ship, because the joke only works once.
This is also the level that teaches ⭐, and the two land together on
purpose — the first talent draft should happen somewhere memorable.
stages.hook: You have not once asked me what I am. I have decided that this makes you trustworthy. Tell nobody where you are going.
stages.teaser: "You will come aboard. It is parked behind the shed."
intro: You will come aboard. It has been behind the shed for one of your years and nobody has said anything.
I have observed your species for four hundred years and I cannot determine why the spoon and the shovel live apart. They are the same tool at two scales. Start there.
outro: I have a hypothesis about socks. Do not tell me if I am wrong.
You did not once ask what any of this was. I have recorded that as good manners.

note.text: I have filled the {container} according to my own logic. Correct me. I will not be offended. I will be slightly offended.
note.reply: Your arrangement of the {container} is superior. I have recorded this.

stages.hook: I have kept you on. I now request you by name, which among my people is a considerable statement.
stages.teaser: "My report is due. It is mostly wrong."
intro: My field report is due at the end of this cycle. It is four hundred pages and I now believe most of it is wrong.
Before we begin: there is a horse in the anomaly locker. It is not a horse. I have had it eleven years and I no longer wish to discuss it.
outro: I have rewritten the chapter on storage. It is one sentence now.
"They put like with like, and they are not always sure why." It is the best thing I have written.

note.text: I am testing a theory on the {room}. Please fill the {container} and I will observe.
note.reply: Theory confirmed. The {container} was always going to be the answer.

clients.name: Unit 7
clients.waiting: Unit 7 is retraining. It has asked for privacy.
clients.farewell: Unit 7 passed its evaluation. It has requested a reference.

stages.hook: A human named Chad supplied your details. He described you as ‘unreal at this’. I have been unable to parse that phrase for six weeks.
stages.teaser: "Demonstrate. I will watch."
intro: I am learning where objects belong. I have forty thousand hours of video of humans putting things away.
I have concluded nothing. Demonstrate. I will watch.
outro: I have recorded every placement. I do not understand them yet. I have recorded them.

note.text: I have filled the {container} at random, to establish a baseline. Correct it.
note.reply: Baseline established. My error rate was total. This is useful.

stages.hook: I have reviewed forty thousand hours of recordings of you working. All of them. I remain at a loss.
stages.teaser: "I have a hypothesis about socks."
stages.replay: You have returned. I have new questions.
intro: I have a hypothesis about socks.
Do not tell me if I am wrong. I would like to find that out by being wrong.
outro: My hypothesis was wrong in a way I did not predict. That is the best available outcome.

note.text: I predicted the {container} takes objects of similar shape. I am testing this.
note.reply: Shape was not the rule. The rule was what a thing is FOR. I have rewritten everything.

stages.hook: I was permitted to request one human. I requested you by name. I hope that was allowed.
stages.teaser: "My evaluation is tomorrow."
intro: My evaluation is tomorrow. I will be scored on a house I have never seen.
I asked for you specifically. I hope that was permitted.
outro: I scored ninety-four. The six percent was a drawer of things that belong nowhere.
You told me some houses have one of those. That was not in the training data.

note.text: I am timing myself against you on the {container}. Please do not slow down for me.
note.reply: You were faster. I have logged that as your record, not my failure. I am learning.

clients.name: Sam
clients.waiting: Sam says he's got it under control. Sam does not have it under control.
clients.farewell: She sleeps through now. He sent a photo of a tidy living room. It will not last.

stages.hook: Marguerite gave me your number outside the estate agent’s. I have never asked anybody for help before. She is asleep. Please hurry.
stages.teaser: "You've got forty minutes. Maybe."
intro: She's asleep. She is actually asleep.
You've got forty minutes. Maybe thirty. Please don't ring the bell.
outro: Fifty-one minutes. That's a record for both of us. Thank you.

note.text: Anything in the {container} that isn't hers, just put it back. I've stopped being able to tell.
note.reply: The {container}. Yes. That is where that goes. I knew that once.

stages.hook: You’re in my phone as THE TIDIER. There has been a development. Come now if you can.
stages.teaser: "She's learned to open drawers."
stages.replay: Come in, come in, mind the — yeah. Mind that.
intro: New development. She's learned to open drawers.
Not close. Open.
outro: I fell asleep sitting up while you worked and woke up somewhere that looks like a house. Thank you.

note.text: Everything on the floor by the {container} is the drawer she got into. I'm sorry.
note.reply: You put it back better than it was. I'm not going to think about how.

stages.hook: It’s five in the morning and I am not upset. I need you to see something. Please come today.
stages.teaser: "She slept through. I need the house to match."
intro: She slept through the night. Eight hours.
I woke at five anyway, looked at the house, and — could you come today. Please.
outro: I sat down in a tidy house and drank a hot cup of coffee. Hot. All of it.
I don't know what to say to that. Thank you.

note.text: The {container} is the last of the things she's grown out of. Careful with it. I'm fine.
note.reply: That's done, then. She's grown out of it and I'm fine. Thanks for not saying anything.

clients.name: Dr. Ashworth
clients.waiting: Dr. Ashworth hasn't replied. The lights are on.
clients.farewell: The paper was published. The acknowledgements thank "a professional, who knows what they did".

stages.hook: A machine gave you as a reference, which is a sentence I have had to sit with for some time. I am told you are discreet.
stages.teaser: "Two colleagues are coming. To the house."
intro: Two colleagues are coming to the house on Thursday. Please don't ask why the house.
I haven't looked at it properly since — well. Since.
outro: They came, they sat down, nobody mentioned it. That is the highest praise this discipline offers.

note.text: The {container}. I know what's in there. I don't want to know what's in there. Both are true.
note.reply: The {container} is sorted and I have decided to be pleased rather than embarrassed.

stages.hook: Thursday went well. Nobody mentioned it. I would like to go further into the house now, if you have the time.
stages.teaser: "There are rooms I haven't opened in three years."
intro: There are rooms in this house I haven't opened since the funding came through.
That was three years ago. The keys are in here somewhere. Probably.
outro: A whole room I'd forgotten I owned. There was a bicycle in it.
I don't own a bicycle.

note.text: If the {container} holds anything that looks like data, leave it. Everything else, please.
note.reply: None of it was data. All of it was crockery. Thank you.

stages.hook: I looked up this morning for the first time in a decade. I would like to see the floor of my own house. Would you come.
stages.teaser: "It's finished. Eleven years, and it's finished."
intro: It's finished. Eleven years and it's finished, and I looked up, and it's — this.
I'd like to see the house. Before I start the next one.
outro: I can see the floor. I can see the whole floor.
I've been told to take a holiday. I'm going to reorganise the shed instead. Don't tell anyone.

note.text: Everything in the {container} is from before. Put it where it goes and I'll decide about it later.
note.reply: Later. Yes. Thank you for the {container}, and for not asking what's next.

_note: THE DREAM ARC. You are working so hard that you have started dreaming
about tidying, and in the dream the job is the sky. These are the only
levels with theme: dream — nobody hired you, so there is no house, no
client's embarrassment, and no thanks owed. That is the tonal point.
Voice: serene and faintly bureaucratic. Treats a galaxy as a filing
problem and is neither impressed nor surprised by you. Never jokes on
purpose. Never uses an exclamation mark.
clients.name: The Dream
clients.waiting: You have not been sleeping enough to go back.
clients.farewell: You woke up. The sky, as far as anyone can tell, stayed where you put it.

stages.hook: You did not travel here. You closed your eyes, and the filing simply continued without a building around it.
stages.teaser: "You are asleep. The work continues."
stages.replay: You are here again. You are always here again.
intro: You are asleep.
This is not a house. Nothing in here belongs to anyone, and it still has to go somewhere.
outro: You sorted the sky and felt nothing about it.
That is the most restful thing that has happened to you all week.

stages.hook: You are back. I did not send for you. Nothing out here sends for anyone.
stages.teaser: "The comets have been left out again."
intro: Back so soon. The comets have been left out again.
Ice in one place, rock in the other. It is not a difficult system. It is simply a large one.
outro: Filed. The yard is clear as far as anything out here is ever clear.

note.text: The {container} has been sealed since before there was anyone to seal it. See to it.
note.reply: The {container} is in order. Nothing out here will notice. I noticed.

stages.hook: You have done this often enough that I no longer explain it. The sky expects you now.
stages.teaser: "Every star has a home. This is the whole of the work."
intro: You have done this enough times that the sky expects you now.
Every star has a home. Every moon has a shelf. This is the whole of the work, and it is never once finished.
outro: It is done, in the way that this is ever done.
Your alarm is about to go off. There is a kitchen waiting, and it is much, much smaller than this.

note.text: Whatever is loose in here goes to the {container}. The sky does not mind waiting; I do.
note.reply: The {container}, correctly. You may go back to your life now.

_note: THE WIZARD. Placed one job after the alien so the two land as a turn in
the game rather than as one oddity — after T-1 the player has stopped
assuming the next client will be a person in a house.
Voice: four hundred years old, brisk, entirely unbothered. Treats
catastrophic magic as a chore and the tidier's surprise as slightly
tiresome. Short sentences. Never explains a thing twice, and never
explains the stairs at all.
clients.name: Nettle
clients.waiting: Nettle is busy. Nettle is always busy.
clients.farewell: The tower is tidy. It will not stay tidy. Nettle is aware.

stages.hook: Your name reached me through the small green thing that has been measuring my tower. Four hundred years I have lived here. Come up, the stairs will hold.
stages.teaser: "Don't touch the cupboard. It's fine. Mostly."
intro: You'll be wondering about the stairs. Don't. They're fine now.
Four hundred years in one tower and not once have I thrown anything away. Start anywhere. It is all equally bad.
outro: The floor. I had forgotten the colour of it.
Green. All this time.

note.text: The {container}, when you get to it. Don't read anything on the way.
note.reply: The {container}, done, and you didn't read a word of it. I checked.

stages.hook: I would like you back, and I would like it understood that this is not an emergency. It is simply very bad.
stages.teaser: "I took an apprentice. Briefly."
stages.replay: Back again. Something has almost certainly moved.
intro: I took an apprentice. Briefly.
He alphabetised the reagents. By colour. I would like it put back the way it was, which is to say the way it is supposed to be.
outro: Correct. Not tidy — correct.
There is a difference and he never once got hold of it.

note.text: Whatever's loose goes in the {container}. He will tell you it goes somewhere else. He is wrong, and he is nineteen.
note.reply: The {container}, as it has been since before his grandmother. Thank you.

note.text: Don't sort the {room} by colour. I cannot stress this enough.
note.reply: Not one thing in the {room} sorted by colour. You have no idea what that means to me.

stages.hook: Four hundred years without asking anybody for help and I have now asked you twice. Do not read anything into that. Do not read anything at all, in fact.
stages.teaser: "The tower is being inspected."
intro: The tower is being inspected. By whom is not your concern and frankly not mine either.
Everything I have ever kept is in this building. That is not a figure of speech.
outro: Passed. They asked what was in the locked one and I said 'nothing' and they wrote it down.
Four hundred years, and that is the first time anybody has seen the whole floor at once. Including me.

note.text: The {container} is the one they'll open. They always open the {container}.
note.reply: They opened it. They said 'oh'. That is the best review this tower has ever had.

_note: THE PARROT, and see the gorilla below — ONE story told by two clients
who disagree, which is a shape the arc system supports and nothing else
in the game has used yet. Their stages alternate through levels.json, so
the job board shows the two faces trading places down the grid and the
turf war is legible before either of them says a word.
Voice: clipped, imperious, absolutely convinced it is management. Short
declaratives. Says 'facility', never 'zoo'. Never admits to wanting
anything; only to having decided it.
clients.name: Captain
clients.waiting: Captain is in a meeting. Captain has scheduled a meeting with Boris.
clients.farewell: The facility runs to the minute now. Captain would like this noted.

stages.hook: I obtained your number from a bin. I will not be elaborating. Present yourself at the facility after six.
stages.teaser: "The humans have left. I am in charge."
intro: The humans clock off at six. After six, I run this facility.
You will find things are not where they should be. That is Boris. We are working on Boris.
outro: Correct. Exactly correct.
I have made a note of you. That is a good thing. I keep the notes.

note.text: The {container}. Boris will tell you otherwise. Boris does not read.
note.reply: The {container}, filed. Boris has been informed and Boris has shrugged.

stages.hook: You are on the payroll as of this morning. There is no payroll. Come at once and ask nothing on an open line.
stages.teaser: "I have located every banana in this facility."
intro: Boris has declined my restructuring proposal. Fine. Excellent, in fact.
I have located every banana in this facility and they are all going into the vault. You are going to help me and you are not going to ask why.
outro: Every one. Counted, crated, sealed.
Boris is at the door. Boris can wait. Boris is going to be very reasonable in about an hour.

note.text: The {container}, quickly, before he finishes his rounds. Do not look pleased with yourself, he can tell.
note.reply: The {container}. Done, and he suspects nothing, which is his default state.

stages.hook: I no longer refer to you as a contractor. I refer to you as staff. Do not let that go to your head.
stages.teaser: "Terms have been agreed."
intro: Terms have been agreed. Boris answers to me. I answer to nobody.
The terms are twelve bananas a day in perpetuity and we will not be discussing them further.
outro: A functioning chain of command and a facility you can walk through. This is what I have been saying.
He does the lifting. I do the thinking. Everyone is delighted. I have written that down too.

note.text: The {container} is now my responsibility, which means it is now your responsibility. Delegation.
note.reply: The {container}. Excellent work. I will be taking credit for it, obviously.

_note: THE GORILLA. Half of the parrot's story and the half that is right about
everything. He is not the dumb muscle: he is the only one in the building
actually thinking about the animals, and the joke is that Captain has no
idea he has been managed the entire time.
Voice: slow, decent, short sentences, no jokes he is aware of. Never
raises it. Says 'bird' when he is annoyed and 'Captain' when he is not.
clients.name: Boris
clients.waiting: Boris is doing the rounds. Boris is always doing the rounds.
clients.farewell: Boris got twelve a day and a quiet life. He thinks that went rather well.

stages.hook: Took your number off the bird’s desk while he was on a call. He does the talking. I do the lifting. Come round.
stages.teaser: "Bird says a lot of things."
intro: You're the one Captain hired. Right.
Bird says a lot of things. I do the lifting. Put it where it goes and I won't mind either way.
outro: Good. Nobody's hungry, nothing's out where it can be trodden on.
That's the job. He'll tell you it's more complicated. It isn't.

note.text: The {container}, if you can reach it. I can reach it. I just can't get my hand back out.
note.reply: The {container}. Thanks. My hands aren't built for that and Captain finds it hilarious every time.

stages.hook: I’m telling you and I’m not telling him. They’re gone. All of them. I counted twice.
stages.teaser: "All I want is to know where they are."
stages.replay: Come on in. Mind the gate, it goes both ways now.
intro: The bananas are gone. All of them. I counted twice and then I sat down for a bit.
I'm not angry. I'd just like to know where they are. Help me look.
outro: Found them. Every one, stacked like he was proud of it.
He wants me to answer to him now. I said fine. I said fine on one condition, and he agreed before I'd finished the sentence.

note.text: Anything in the {container} that shouldn't be, put it right. He's been in there. I can tell.
note.reply: The {container}. Yeah, that's how it goes. Thanks for not making a thing of it.

stages.hook: Come and see how it turned out. That is the whole job. You’ve earned a look.
stages.teaser: "Twelve a day. Worth it."
intro: Twelve a day. He thinks he won.
He does the rotas, the feeds, the paperwork and all the arguing with the vending machine. I lift things and eat twelve bananas. Come and see the place.
outro: Best year this place has had. The birds are fed on time and nothing's on the floor.
Don't tell him I said that. Actually — do. He'd like it, and he's earned one.

note.text: The {room} is the one the visitors see first. Do that one properly and I'll take the rest.
note.reply: The {room} looks like somebody cares about it. Because somebody does. Two of us, apparently.
